newsitem.title: USA: CALENERGY GETS STATE OK FOR NYSEG TENDER.
newsitem.headline: CALENERGY GETS STATE OK FOR NYSEG TENDER.

text.p: The New York Public Service Commission said Wednesday it would permit independent power producer CalEnergy Co Inc to proceed with a tender offer for 9.9 percent of New York State Electric & Gas Corp.
In a statement announcing its decision, the state regulators said it had determined the tender offer "poses no threat to rate payers and does benefit the holders of the stock in question."
NYSEG had asked the commission to prohibit the $24.50 per share tender offer from proceeding.
CalEnergy has launched the $159 million tender offer as the first step of a plan to buy the whole utility in a transaction valued at $1.9 billion.

In seeking to block the tender offer, which expires on Thursday, NYSEG had cited a portion of the state's Public Service Law, which it contended requires companies to receive commission approval before acquiring securities of a gas or electric company.
CalEnergy had argued it was entitled to buy less than 10 percent of NYSEG without prior commission approval.
The order officially was issued by commission Chairman John O'Mara and will be presented to the full commission for approval on August 20.
Although the order approved the purchase of 9.9 percent of NYSEG shares, it also noted that the approval is separate from any future decisions about a NYSEG takeover.

"Any future commission analysis of additional purchases will address, among other things, the far more complex issue of whether the public interest will be served by CalEnergy's management of NYSEG," the commission said.
It also ordered CalEnergy to file for approval of any additional share purchases by no later than August 29.

CalEnergy Chief Executive Officer David Sokol said the company will not extend the tender offer past Thursday's deadline and will walk away from the transaction if it does not receive shareholder support.
"If shareholders voice their opinion that we are not the right acquiror, then we respect that and move on," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I think our hope is that NYSEG will stop trying to put roadblocks in front of the shareholders so that they can accept our tender offer, or not, tomorrow," he said.
He also reiterated that CalEnergy would prefer a friendly transaction with NYSEG as opposed to the hostile approach.
NYSEG last month rejected the CalEnergy offer and last week told shareholders it would soon review its dividend policy and stock buyback plans.
NYSEG did not have an immediate comment on the decision.
